Dawei Sun Blog
About
From Words to Waypoints: Teaching a Small LLM to Plan for Robots
Large language models are increasingly asked to act as the high-level planner of a robot: given a task in words or in a formal language, decide where to go, in which order, and when. For tasks written in temporal logic, the classical approach is to encode the whole problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and hand it to a solver. That works, but it can take a very long time, and the cost grows quickly with the length of the task and the number of conditions. A MILP solver is a powerful but blind search: every operator, at every time step, becomes a set of binary variables and constraints, and the solver has no notion of…
